title: Single & SingleOrDefault
description: Learn to retrieve a single element from collections using Single and SingleOrDefault.

data.text: The `Single` and `SingleOrDefault` methods return a single element from a collection. They are stricter than `First` and `Last` — they throw an exception if the collection contains more than one element.
The `Single` method returns the only element from a collection. If the collection is empty or contains more than one element, it throws an `InvalidOperationException`.

data.title: Single Examples

data.text: The `SingleOrDefault` method returns the only element, or the default value if the collection is empty. However, it still throws an exception if the collection contains more than one element.

data.title: SingleOrDefault Examples
Strict Behavior
data.text: Single and SingleOrDefault throw an exception if there are multiple matching elements. Use FirstOrDefault if you only need the first match.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Single returns the only element from a collection
Single throws if collection is empty or has multiple elements
SingleOrDefault returns default if empty, throws if multiple
Useful when you expect exactly one match
data.takeaway: Continue to the next module to learn about partitioning operators.
